nodes.label: Ultimate POS 7.3
nodes.rationale: A viable host for SaverBro Recommerce OS because its Laravel monolith already owns the business-critical ledgers - products/variations, purchase and sale transactions, location quantity, FIFO/LIFO cost mapping, transfers, payments, contacts, roles, printing and activity logging.

nodes.label: No serialized-asset identity
nodes.rationale: Ultimate POS is quantity-led: it has no unique physical-unit record, no serial uniqueness, no unit ownership/location tracking, and no binding of one device to one purchase/sale/transfer line. A new first-class device domain is therefore required, added as a module and coordinated with - not substituted for - existing POS stock/accounting paths.

nodes.label: Modules/Recommerce implementation home
nodes.rationale: Implement SaverBro functionality as a new module and keep core edits limited to narrowly documented guard/hook points where existing callbacks/events cannot enforce a serialized-stock invariant.

nodes.label: Missing module-source gate
nodes.rationale: config/modules.php declares Modules/ and modules_statuses.json marks Repair enabled, but the directory is absent and public/modules/repair holds zero-byte placeholders while core code references Modules\Repair entities. No claim about the existing Repair module's data model, transitions, quotations, parts or permissions is possible, so implementation must first compare the target architecture against recovered source and write an adopt/adapt/retire decision record.

nodes.label: Modules/Repair licensed module
nodes.rationale: Proven to be expected by core (transactions.sub_type='repair', receipt rendering reaching into RepairStatus and DeviceModel, repair_model_id filters, repair.create permission) but its tables, identifier generation, state machine, quotes, parts, queues and tests cannot be audited from this checkout.

nodes.label: ModuleUtil::getModuleData hook mechanism
nodes.rationale: The main extension mechanism: discovers installed modules, resolves Modules\<Name>\Http\Controllers\DataController and calls named hooks, which is how core screens ask modules for product form fragments, role permissions, sale hooks and invoice QR data.

nodes.label: Product and variation model
nodes.rationale: Product/variation remains the catalog and quantity/accounting identity. A physical device must reference a variation but must not become a new variation per unit, and customer-owned repair devices may have no product/variation until SaverBro acquires them.

nodes.label: Purchase and acquisition model
nodes.rationale: Purchases are transactions with type='purchase'; reaching 'received' increases variation_location_details.qty_available. The fixed additional-expense columns are unsuitable as a permanent device cost ledger, so they remain the invoice summary while recommerce allocates landed cost per device in its own append-only ledger.

nodes.label: Sales, service products and payments
nodes.rationale: A customer repair job links to one Ultimate POS sell transaction; parts use normal stock product lines and labour/diagnosis/outsourced charges use non-stock service products, so Ultimate POS remains the only invoice, tax, cash-register, payment and accounting path.

nodes.label: ProductUtil aggregate stock helpers
nodes.rationale: updateProductQuantity/decreaseProductQuantity mutate variation_location_details.qty_available without locking rows and without knowledge of physical devices. Avoid broad edits - it is central to aggregate stock mutations and reporting.

nodes.label: TransactionUtil
nodes.rationale: Owns sales, payments, cost mapping, receipts and reports, and reaches into Modules\Repair entities for receipt rendering. Avoid broad edits.

nodes.label: FIFO/LIFO purchase-sell cost mapping
nodes.rationale: transaction_sell_lines_purchase_lines allocates sale or adjustment quantity against eligible received purchase lines. Recommerce must not create a second quantity ledger: device records provide the unit-level subledger while aggregate quantity remains Ultimate POS, updated inside one transaction and reconciled.

nodes.label: Stock helpers lack row locking
nodes.rationale: Existing stock helpers take no explicit locks, so the recommerce coordinator must lock device, variation/location and relevant source rows before committing a serialized operation.

nodes.label: StockTransferController paired transfers
nodes.rationale: A transfer creates paired sell_transfer/purchase_transfer transactions linked by transfer_parent_id. The status-update path changes aggregate stock in a transaction but never dispatches the stock-transfer event, so tracked devices passing that route need a minimal core hook or the route must be blocked for serialized variations.

nodes.label: SellPosController finalization path
nodes.rationale: Highly coupled POS finalization - creates sell transaction and lines, writes payments, decrements stock, maps sold quantity to purchase lines, invokes the module after_sale_saved hook inside the transaction, then commits and dispatches SellCreatedOrModified. Touch minimally.

nodes.label: PurchaseController
nodes.rationale: Orchestrates purchase/payment/stock receipt in one database transaction; touch minimally.

nodes.label: enable_sr_no serial support
nodes.rationale: The product flag only exposes the generic transaction_sell_lines.sell_line_note text field, so it is invoice annotation rather than serialized inventory - no serial table, no uniqueness constraint, no purchase-side serial identity, no location/ownership lifecycle.

nodes.label: Lot tracking
nodes.rationale: Lots live on purchase_lines.lot_number and can identify an acquisition batch, but a purchase line may represent many units and therefore cannot be the canonical device.

nodes.label: Barcode, QR and label tooling
nodes.rationale: Reuse label geometry, mPDF, browser print patterns and the barcode/QR libraries, but do not reuse the existing label endpoint/data loop as the device identity implementation because it repeats one variation detail by quantity and cannot emit distinct unit tokens.

nodes.label: Scanning surface
nodes.rationale: Keyboard-emulation scanners can already scan a product SKU through the POS jQuery autocomplete, but there is no global scanner, camera decoder, device/repair resolver, opaque token, or duplicate-scan defense.

nodes.label: Core warranty model
nodes.rationale: A reusable duration definition attached to products and sell lines; it models no claim, repair warranty event, covered device, entitlement consumption or repeat ownership cycle, so use it as a policy/duration source and add entitlements and claims in Recommerce.

nodes.label: Contacts as ownership parties
nodes.rationale: Use the shared supplier/customer party table for suppliers, repair customers, current owners and invoice recipients; do not create a parallel customer master.

nodes.label: Spatie Permission roles
nodes.rationale: Roles are business-scoped and admin receives a gate-wide allow for ordinary abilities; module permissions are injected into the native role editor through DataController::user_permissions. Recommerce abilities must always be combined with business and location predicates - a permission like recommerce.device.view is not sufficient if the device sits at an inaccessible location.

nodes.label: Spatie Activitylog
nodes.rationale: Useful for operator audit but unsuitable as the permanent device lifecycle ledger, because cleanup deletes records older than 365 days.

nodes.label: Events, queues and the outbox recommendation
nodes.rationale: Core defines domain-shaped events but EventServiceProvider registers only payment/account listeners and disables discovery; default queue execution is sync and after_commit is false. Recommerce should write critical device/job events synchronously in the same transaction and use an outbox for optional notifications and PDF generation.

nodes.label: API surface
nodes.rationale: Only authenticated /api/user exists; Passport is installed but no core device/repair API. The Alpha scanner can use authenticated web JSON endpoints with CSRF, and a versioned Passport API can be added later without changing QR identity.

nodes.label: Migration and testing conventions
nodes.rationale: The suite contains only the default example unit and feature tests with testing database settings commented out - no meaningful stock, permission, repair or barcode regression suite exists, so test coverage is essentially absent as a baseline.

nodes.label: Mandatory pre-implementation gates
nodes.rationale: Recover licensed Modules/ source (especially Repair), restore a PHP 8 runtime and run baselines, recover the front-end build manifest before adding camera-scanner dependencies, obtain a sanitized production schema/data profile, decide the cutover policy for existing serialized stock, and rehearse all schema/data changes on a production-like copy.

nodes.label: Evidence and confidence boundary
nodes.rationale: Architecture reconnaissance only: source is confirmed, but installed production schema, database engine/version, live module versions, production configuration, printer behavior, runtime permissions and data quality are not. php was not installed on the inspection host, so Artisan and PHPUnit were never executed, and package.json is absent so a clean front-end rebuild is not demonstrated.
